definition:
A unique identifier for the record within the dataset. 

For more information, see: http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/catalogNumber
The year in which the study reporting the observation was published.

The year(s) during which sampling was conducted. Sampling may have been conducted within a single year (e.g., 2000), continuously over a range of years (e.g., 2000-2003), or during separate years (e.g., 2004|2007).

The integer month in which the event occurred. Examples: 1 (January), 10 (October).

For more information, see:
http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/month
The season during which sampling was performed, as reported in the study.

The season during which sampling was performed, reclassified into 6 categories and defined as follows:

temperate.warm: the description mentions "summer" or "spring" or sampling was conducted in the warmer months in the northern hemisphere (5/6/7/8) or the warmer months in southern hemisphere (11/12/1/2).

temperate.cool: the description mentions "autumn" or "winter" or sampling was conducted in the other months in each respective hemisphere (see above). 

temperate.both: sampling was conducted in both warm and cool months.

tropical.wet, tropical.dry, tropical.both: determined based on the climate of the specific locality and the sampling months.

The name of the country or major administrative unit in which sampling was conducted.

For more information, see: 
http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/country

The name of the next smaller administrative region than country (state, province, canton, department, region, etc.) in which sampling was conducted. 

For more information, see: 
http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/stateProvince

The specific description of the place in which sampling was conducted.

For more information, see: 
http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/stateProvince

The geographic latitude (in decimal degrees) of the geographic center of the locality. Positive values are north of the Equator, negative values are south of it. 

For more information, see: 
http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/decimalLatitude

The geographic longitude (in decimal degrees) of the geographic center of the locality. Positive values are east of the Greenwich Meridian, negative values are west of it. 

For more information, see: 
http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/decimalLongitude
The elevation (m) of the locality. As reported in the study. If sampling was conducted across an elevational range, the median value was entered.
The general ecosystem type containing the community. Classified into 2 categories: terrestrial and aquatic.
The potential sources of disturbances in the environment. As reported in the study.
The general habitat containing the community. As reported in the study.
The general habitat containing the community, reclassified into 12 categories: cave, desert, dune, forest, grassland, mixed.use, pond, river, savanna, shrubland, stream, wetland.
The vertical habitat stratum (e.g., canopy, understorey, ground surface) from which insects would have been collected, often based on the sampling method. As reported in the study.

A description of the methods or protocols used for sampling. 

For more information, see:
http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/samplingProtocol
The sampling method used to observe or collect insects from a community, reclassified into 4 general categories: attraction, human.observation, movement.interception, other.

A group of organisms considered by taxonomists to form a homogeneous unit.

For more information, see: 
http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/Taxon
The lowest taxonomic rank that encompasses all the individuals sampled (e.g., family).

A common or vernacular name.

For more information, see: 
http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/vernacularName
A higher taxonomic grouping that encompasses all the individuals sampled. Most groupings correspond to insect orders (e.g., Lepidoptera).
The property of the community that was measured. 2 categories: abundance and richness.
The level at which the associated measurementValue was measured. 2 categories: total (the total value from combining all samples) and mean (the average value per sample)
The specific diel period during which sampling occurred and which is thus associated with the measurementValue. Classified into 3 categories: day_and_night, day, and night.

The value of the measurement.

For more information, see:
http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/measurementValue

The units associated with measurementUnit.

For more information, see:
http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/measurementUnit
The number of samples from which the associated measurementValue was obtained.
The standard deviation corresponding to the measurementValue for observations where the measurement_level is mean.
A unique number to identify the corresponding publication in the database.

A bibliographic reference for the resource.

For more information, see: 
http://purl.org/dc/terms/bibliographicCitation
Stable identifier derived from catalogNumber.
Stable hash of latitude and longitude; text locality variants at the same coordinates remain aggregated.
Stable hash of the semantic sampling and measurement context, excluding value representation fields.
Latitude and longitude fall within valid geographic ranges.
sample_size is present and greater than zero.
Preferred record for a measurement group; reported mean is preferred over total.
Agreement status for a directly comparable reported mean and total/sample_size pair.
How night_activity_value was obtained.
Reported mean abundance, or total individuals/sample_size for an unpaired derivable total.
Unit associated with night_activity_value.
Within-study rank percentile for comparable activity records when the context contains at least three records; not approved for global magnitude.
Number of records in the within-study relative-activity context.
Always false in this release because cross-study magnitudes are not comparable.
The record can be placed geographically because its coordinates are valid.
